## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Gihiveyyāvacca-sikkhāpada* ("Training rule on serving householders"), designated as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 44, is a disciplinary rule for Buddhist nuns belonging to the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule lays down that a nun who performs domestic service or menial duties for a lay person (*gihi*) commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its associated case narrative is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Within the Pali canon, the rule is closely tied to Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pācittiya 44 and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 44 [SuttaCentral]. Parallels to this regulation are preserved across the monastic codes of several other early Buddhist schools, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 113), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 148), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 142), Mūlasarvāstivāda (extant in Chinese Pc 153 and Tibetan Pc 137), Mahāsaṅghika (Pc 84), and Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Sanskrit Pc 84) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Automated text alignment via DharmaNexus additionally confirms close cross-linguistic correspondences with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus].
